app.title: Hong Kong Decentralized Archive
app.icon-slogan: Hong Kong books. Keep them moving.
app.description: Greetings from the Library! We are Librarians, and we are here to help you discover your next great read. Whether you're searching for resources, reliable information, or something entirely unexpected, we're here to guide you every step of the way. Explore our collection today and find your new favorites!

governing.title: Governing Colour Principle
governing.description: One rule across all badge systems: colour tells users whether they can act. Build every status badge from these six semantic roles.
governing.note: Always pair a badge with a role-specific action prompt. The badge tells users the state; the action tells them what to do next.

colours.title: Colour Scales
colours.description: Brand magenta, rosy ink neutrals, and warm paper legacy neutrals. Starred swatches are the canonical values used in semantic tokens.

tokens.title: Semantic Tokens
tokens.description: Named slots engineers reference in code. If a colour changes, only the token updates; every component stays consistent.

typography.title: Typography
typography.description: Two typefaces. Noto Serif TC for cultural weight — brand name, book titles, headings. IBM Plex Sans for UI clarity and body text. IBM Plex Mono for labels, tokens, and metadata.

typeTokens.title: Type Tokens
typeTokens.description: Engineering tokens for typography, radius, and spacing. Reference these instead of hard-coding values.

radiusTokens.title: Radius Tokens
radiusTokens.description: A small, scalable radius system that keeps labels, cards, and containers visually consistent without over-rounding the interface.

spacingTokens.title: Spacing Tokens
spacingTokens.description: A consistent spacing rhythm for cards, rows, sections, and the layout shell. These tokens pace the interface and reduce visual drift.

statusChip.title: Status Chip
statusChip.description: Small state indicators with semantic colour and a clear, short label. They reveal what a user can do next without adding visual noise.

categoryChip.title: Category Chip
categoryChip.description: Short, metadata-style labels for subject, authorial context, and civic memory. They stay compact and readable across scripts.

bookCard.title: Book Card
bookCard.description: Flexible card system for featured books, recent arrivals, and topical shelf lists. The content can vary by language, but the card structure remains fixed.

newUserVillage.step1Title: A0仔: X, I want to borrow this book, but it is currently checked out
newUserVillage.step1Body:
A0仔 sees the book: "This is a good one, but someone is borrowing it right now."

No need to get upset. Just tap Request to Borrow.

Then both Ba打 and A0仔 will receive a BookGuide email:
"Hey, someone wants to borrow your book."
After that, both sides can work out the handover themselves — where and when to meet, who brings it, and how to coordinate.
newUserVillage.step2Body:
Finally the time is set.

Ba打 sees A0仔 and passes over the book.

Ba打 taps Face-to-face Handover.

A0仔: 
"Scan the QR code."
After scanning, take a photo to record the book condition at the moment of handover.

That completes the transfer and avoids future arguments:
"You damaged this book!"
"What? It was already like that when I received it."
With photos as proof, everyone stays happy.
newUserVillage.step3Title: C姐: X, turns out I want to read it too
newUserVillage.step3Body:
Later, C姐 sees: 

"Oh wow, I want to read this too."
She can tap Request to Borrow again.

After A0仔 finishes reading it, A0仔 can contact C姐 directly:
"I have finished it. Do you want it?"
Then they arrange another handover time.

And so the book continues circulating:

Ba打 → A0仔 → C姐 → D露霧 → ……

A book does not have to sit trapped in one person's hands forever. Once it is read, pass it to the next person.
